summary: Rules-clean, cheap and readable from the _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel rows, but both mechanisms are weak. The masked activation loads are already 16-byte vectorized, because the mask is constant along the contiguous K axis. DRAM traffic is about 0.2 TB/s, so L2 eviction priority has little to save. evict_first on weights also cuts against the kernel's own token-tile-fastest swizzle. Expect flat to a few %. Rebase on a81d19c and build an in-prepare() A/B of master / unmasked / unmasked+hints so that one check attributes the result.
justification: Profile (FINDINGS): _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel x2 is 8084-9174 us per first_turn shape (37-57% of the shape), and stays on Triton because the CUDA wgmma replacement is dead (LESSONS 2026-10-25: 1.8x slower, spills). The hedge condition in the risk note is therefore met. Persistent A/B (5d9ddbbaaffd4599 log): w13 3059 us and w2 1580 us at T=16384, BLOCK_T=256, with 74 live token tiles. The persistent grid was 2.9%/4.7% slower, so grid shape and dead CTAs are not the limiter, and the original launch order is worth something (L2 locality from the GROUP_SIZE_T swizzle). Rough roofline for w13: about 18.9K sorted rows x N 8192 x K 4096 x 2 is about 1.27 TFLOP in 3.06 ms, about 415 TFLOPS, which is tensor/issue-bound (synchronous tl.dot plus in-register dequant). DRAM is roughly 150 MB of activations plus the expert weights, about 0.2-0.3 TB/s, so L2 residency hints (which only change DRAM refetch) have little to save. L2-to-SM traffic is substantial (about 3 MB per CTA x 4736 CTAs), but evict hints do not reduce it. Mechanism (1): the a_lo/a_hi mask is token_mask[None, :], constant along dim 0, which is the K-contiguous axis (offs_h). Triton's axis analysis therefore already emits 16-byte cp.async with a zero-fill predicate, and dropping the mask saves only per-vector predicate setup, not vectorization. Mechanism (2): the kernel comment says 'token tiles fastest within a group, so the token tiles of one (expert, weight tile) run adjacent and the weight tile is re-read from L2'. evict_first on b/s therefore marks exactly the lines the swizzle is designed to re-hit, so the hint could cost rather than help. Activations already get a 64-way (w13) or 32-way (w2) reuse within a GROUP_SIZE_T=4 group of about 8 MB, which fits L2 without help. WEAKEST LINK: neither sub-change targets the measured limiter (tensor issue / dequant ALU interleave). The most plausible real effect is a side effect: the BLOCK_T=256 variant shows n_regs=254 with n_spills=4, and removing the mask and 'other' operands can change register allocation and remove those spills. That is a legitimate gain, but it is not the stated mechanism. The expected 0-2.5% per first_turn shape is below headline drift (CI ±1.5%), so judge only on the two kernel rows (Triton rows reproduce within ~1%).
confounders: stack-tonight-five-prefill (landed, current master a81d19c): the spec says 'Built on master (635cfee)', but 635cfee is the submission blob of b92a0f4, one promotion behind. The stack changed the first_turn align (moe-align-32-experts-first-turn: different sorted_ids/padding layout and fewer -1 blocks) and turned w2 ZERO_NONLOCAL off. Both change what the K loop sees: the number of padding columns per tile, and early exits. Building on the stale base would measure a different padding mix, so it must rebase onto a81d19c.

experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256: it set BLOCK_T=256 at T > 4096 (254 regs, 4 spills). Any register change from removing the mask lands on a config that is at the register cap, so a gain may come from spill removal, not from load predication or L2. Read the n_regs/n_spills log line against master's (254/4) before attributing.
experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn: gates the Triton kernel to T > 4096 only; turn shapes stay on Marlin, so 'turn_* neutral' is structurally guaranteed.
interference: No separate companion run. The two sub-changes could have opposite signs (unmasked loads/spills help; evict_first on weights hurts the swizzle's reuse), so a flat result alone would be ambiguous. The cheap fix belongs inside this run, as the persistent-grid hypothesis already did: prepare() times master's kernel, unmasked-only and unmasked+hints at T=16384 for w13 and w2. Use graph replays with 7 alternations, print '[loads A/B] ... ratio' lines, ship the fastest variant only if its ratio is <= 0.98, and otherwise keep master's kernel. Prepare timings undercount the profile by 20-25% but rank correctly (LESSONS 2026-10-25). Also print n_regs/n_spills for each variant. That resolves attribution at zero extra checks; a companion run would only re-measure the same rows with more noise.
rules_flags: None blocking. The padding columns now read activation row 0 (in bounds), and their products go only to output columns that the masked store drops. The output store keeps mask=token_mask, and -1 expert blocks still return early. safe_token = tl.where(token_mask, offs_token, 0) must be computed from the int64 offs_token before the // TOP_K.
Eviction hints are cache policy, not caching of input-derived results, so they are allowed. No host sync is added. Any prepare-time A/B timing must stay in prepare(), never in kernel_fn.
open_questions: Does Triton actually emit predicated 16-byte cp.async for the masked a loads today? Dump the TTGIR/PTX once in prepare() (ld/cp.async width) to settle mechanism (1).
Do n_spills on the BLOCK_T=256 variant drop from 4 to 0 with unmasked loads? If yes, that is the likely source of any gain.
Is evict_first on b/s harmful given the token-tile-fastest swizzle? The in-prepare three-way A/B answers this directly.
